Ordinances for the Prince and the Priests.</title> <div sID="gen21457" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11869"/><hi type="bold">2. shut ... not be opened--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Job.12.14">Job 12:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.22.22">Is 22:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.3.7">Re 3:7</reference>). "Shut" to the people (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.21">Ex 19:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.19.22">22</reference>), but open to "the prince" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.44.3">Eze 44:3</reference>), he holding the place of God in political concerns, as the priests do in spiritual. As a mark of respect to an Eastern monarch, the gate by which he enters is thenceforth shut to all other persons (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.19.24">Ex 19:24</reference>). <div eID="gen21457" type="x-p"/>

As a mark of respect to an Eastern monarch, the gate by which he enters is thenceforth shut to all other persons (compare Ex 19:24 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11870"/><div sID="gen21458" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11870"/><hi type="bold">3. the prince--</hi>not King Messiah, as He never would offer a burnt offering for Himself, as the prince is to do (<reference osisRef="Ezek.46.4">Eze 46:4</reference>). The prince must mean the civil ruler under Messiah. His connection with the east gate (by which the Lord had returned to His temple) implies, that, as ruling under God, he is to stand in a place of peculiar nearness to God. He represents Messiah, who entered heaven, the true sanctuary, by a way that none other could, namely, by His own holiness; all others must enter as sinners by faith in His blood, through grace.<div eID="gen21458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21459" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eat bread before the Lord--</hi>a custom connected with sacrifices (<reference osisRef="Gen.31.54">Ge 31:54</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.18.12">Ex 18:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.24.11">24:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.10.18">1Co 10:18</reference>). <div eID="gen21459" type="x-p"/>

Directions as to the priests. Their acts of desecration are attributed to "the house of Israel" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.44.6">Eze 44:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.44.7">7</reference>), as the sins of the priesthood and of the people acted and reacted on one another; "like people, like priest" (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.31">Jr 5:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.4.9">Ho 4:9</reference>). <div eID="gen21460" type="x-p"/>

Levites ... shall ... bear--</hi>namely, the punishment of<div eID="gen21464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21465" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their iniquity ... Yet they shall be ministers--</hi>So Mark, a Levite, nephew of Barnabas (<reference osisRef="Acts.4.36">Ac 4:36</reference>), was punished by Paul for losing an opportunity of bearing the cross of Christ, and yet was afterwards admitted into his friendship again, and showed his zeal (<reference osisRef="Acts.13.13">Ac 13:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.15.37">15:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.4.10">Col 4:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Tim.4.11">2Ti 4:11</reference>). One may be a believer, and that too in a distinguished place, and yet lose some special honor--be acknowledged as pious, yet be excluded from some dignity [Bengel].<div eID="gen21465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21466" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">charge at the gates--</hi>Better to be "a doorkeeper in the house of God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness" (<reference osisRef="Ps.84.10">Psa 84:10</reference>). Though standing as a mere doorkeeper, it is in the house of God, which hath foundations: whereas he who dwells with the wicked, dwells in but shifting tents. <div eID="gen21466" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 10-11. Levites ... shall ... bear-- namely, the punishment of their iniquity ... Yet they shall be ministers-- So Mark, a Levite, nephew of Barnabas ( Ac 4:36 ), was punished by Paul for losing an opportunity of bearing the cross of Christ, and yet was afterwards admitted into his friendship again, and showed his zeal ( Ac 13:13 ; 15:37 ; Col 4:10 ; 2Ti 4:11 ). One may be a believer, and that too in a distinguished place, and yet lose some special honor--be acknowledged as pious, yet be excluded from some dignity [Bengel]. charge at the gates-- Better to be "a doorkeeper in the house of God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness" ( Psa 84:10 ). Though standing as a mere doorkeeper, it is in the house of God, which hath foundations: whereas he who dwells with the wicked, dwells in but shifting tents.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11875"/><div sID="gen21467" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11875"/><hi type="bold">15. Zadok--</hi>The priests of the line of Ithamar were to be discharged from ministrations in the temple, because of their corruptions, following in the steps of Eli's sons, against whom the same denunciation was uttered (<reference osisRef="1Sam.2.32">1Sa 2:32</reference>, 35). Zadok, according to his name (which means "righteous") and his line, were to succeed (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.2.35">1Ki 2:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.3">1Ch 24:3</reference>), as they did not take part in the general apostasy to the same degree, and perhaps [Fairbairn] the prophet, referring to their original state, speaks of them as they appeared when first chosen to the office. <div eID="gen21467" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 15. Zadok-- The priests of the line of Ithamar were to be discharged from ministrations in the temple, because of their corruptions, following in the steps of Eli's sons, against whom the same denunciation was uttered ( 1Sa 2:32 , 35). Zadok, according to his name (which means "righteous") and his line, were to succeed ( 1Ki 2:35 ; 1Ch 24:3 ), as they did not take part in the general apostasy to the same degree, and perhaps [Fairbairn] the prophet, referring to their original state, speaks of them as they appeared when first chosen to the office.
